item.text: I’ll add only omitted connections that are clear from the brief and my remembered coverage, without reopening either file.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat > /Volumes/aro/projects/prose_generation/enrichment/bible/work/s103/discovery/s103-20261009/sec15/luna/followup.tsv <<'FOLLOWUP_TSV'
strong	tevrat	paralel	WLC:Gen.40.23	Joseph forgotten in confinement	The commentary pairs Joseph’s prison with patience; after the cupbearer is restored, he forgets Joseph, adding the concrete delay of being left confined and unremembered.
strong	tevrat	paralel	WLC:Gen.41.1	Two years pass before Joseph is recalled	The commentary makes detention and patience meet; Genesis marks two full years before Pharaoh’s dream brings the imprisoned Joseph back into view, specifying the length of the wait.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.47.29	A dying patriarch asks for an oath about burial	The commentary’s testament scene joins approaching death, trust, and obligation; Jacob, near death, asks Joseph to swear that he will not bury him in Egypt.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.47.31	The deathbed request is secured by an oath	The commentary places oath and bequest together at death; Joseph swears to Jacob’s burial request, turning a dying person’s instruction into an entrusted duty.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.50.25	A final oath entrusted to the next generation	The commentary joins death, custody, and what passes between people; Joseph makes Israel’s descendants swear to carry his bones when God visits them.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.1.16	Fire consumes accumulated flocks and servants	The commentary’s ruined garden includes a destructive fiery storm; in Job’s sequence of calamities, fire from heaven consumes sheep and servants, one part of the sudden loss of his holdings.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.90.12	Numbering days to gain wisdom	The commentary treats time as expiring capital; the psalm asks to be taught to number one’s days so the heart may gain wisdom, turning limited time into a prompt for action.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.1.2	Meditating on instruction day and night	The commentary says communal counsel joins like night and day; the psalmist meditates on Torah day and night, making ethical instruction a sustained practice across time.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.1.3	A righteous tree bears fruit in season and does not wither	The commentary’s fruitful garden is destroyed at the moment of expected yield; Psalm 1 pictures the righteous as a watered tree whose seasonal fruit remains, a counter-image of stability.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Amos.8.2	Summer fruit announces the end	The commentary layers ripe produce with life’s late hour and the end of time; Amos’s basket of summer fruit signals that Israel’s end has arrived, making harvest itself an omen of ending.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.40.8	Human growth fades while the word endures	The commentary moves from mortal time to truth that is transmitted and kept; Isaiah contrasts fading grass and flowers with the enduring word of God.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.3.3	Truth bound at the neck and written on the heart	The commentary joins truth to holding and binding; Proverbs tells the reader to bind faithfulness and truth around the neck and write them on the heart, combining tethering with inward preservation.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.6.1	A person becomes surety for a neighbor	The commentary gives patience the secondary image of a guarantor and joins trust to debt; Proverbs depicts someone pledging security for a neighbor, making the guarantee a concrete accepted burden.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Exod.22.26	A pledged garment returned before sunset	The commentary joins debt, holding, and release within passing time; Exodus requires a creditor to return a poor borrower’s garment by sunset, so the pledge cannot become lasting captivity.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.15.14	A freed servant sent away with produce	The commentary defines the ascent through freeing a captive and feeding the hungry; Deuteronomy says not to send a released servant away empty-handed but to provide from flock, threshing floor, and winepress.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:2Kgs.4.1	A creditor threatens to take a widow’s sons as slaves	The commentary brings debt and release from captivity together; the widow’s unpaid debt puts her sons at risk of enslavement, making the financial obligation a threat to family freedom.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:2Kgs.4.7	Oil sold to pay debt and preserve a livelihood	The commentary’s debt and release scenes meet in Elisha’s instruction: the widow sells the multiplied oil, pays the creditor, and lives on what remains.
strong	tevrat	motif	Sirach 29:15	Remember the one who stood as guarantor	The commentary calls patience a guarantor; Sirach warns not to forget the kindness of one who guaranteed a neighbor’s debt and risked much on that person’s behalf.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.7.22	Jesus as guarantor of a better covenant	The commentary’s secondary guarantor image meets Hebrews’ explicit description of Jesus as guarantor, applying financial surety language to the covenant.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.1.13	Truth heard, believed, and sealed	The commentary gathers belief, truth, and what is kept; Ephesians says its readers heard the word of truth, believed, and were sealed with the promised Spirit.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.1.14	A seal that guarantees inheritance	The commentary calls patience a guarantor and ends with what is preserved; Ephesians calls the Spirit the guarantee of inheritance until redemption.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.4.2	Patience expressed by bearing with one another	The commentary turns patience into reciprocal communal counsel; Paul joins humility, patience, and bearing with one another in love.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.4.3	Unity held by a bond of peace	The commentary pictures people holding together; Paul urges preservation of the Spirit’s unity through a bond of peace.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.13.6	Love rejoices with truth	The commentary makes truth the content of mutual counsel; Paul says love rejoices with the truth, placing truthful conduct inside communal ethics.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.13.7	Love bears and endures all things	The commentary presents patience as a quality exchanged within the community; Paul describes love as bearing and enduring all things, a sustained communal form of sabr.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.2.7	Patient persistence in good work	The commentary’s exception to loss joins belief, good deeds, and patience; Paul describes those who persist patiently in good work as seeking glory and eternal life.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.3.13	Daily mutual exhortation prevents hardening	The commentary’s community advises one another; Hebrews commands daily encouragement so that no one is hardened by sin’s deceit, specifying both the repeated action and its danger.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.10.36	Endurance after doing God’s will	The commentary closes with good action and patience held together; Hebrews says endurance is needed after doing God’s will in order to receive what is promised.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.12.1	Lay aside weight and run with endurance	The commentary makes the steep ascent a road with a load; Hebrews tells runners to lay aside every weight and run the set race with endurance.
strong	tevrat	motif	Mishnah Avot 4:11	Good deeds as advocates and a shield	The commentary says deeds distinguish those who escape loss; Avot pictures a commandment as an advocate and repentance with good deeds as a shield against punishment.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.119.11	The word stored in the heart	The commentary ends with truth received and preserved; the psalmist stores God’s word in the heart as a safeguard against sin, making inward keeping an ethical act.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.5.16	Time treated as something to redeem	The commentary calls time capital that can be spent or lost; Paul urges believers to make the most of the time because the days are evil, giving time an explicit economic value.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.14.19	Ripe grapes cast into the winepress of judgment	The commentary layers fruit, pressing, and the end; Revelation gathers ripe grapes and casts them into God’s great winepress, making the press a harvest image of judgment.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.15.58	Steadfast work is not in vain	The commentary says most human effort is loss but closes with faithful work and patience; Paul calls believers steadfast and abundant in the Lord’s work, assuring them that such labor is not empty.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.13.8	One more year for a fruitless tree	The commentary overlaps orchard, aging time, and the risk of losing fruit; the gardener asks for one more year to tend the barren fig tree, making patience a limited extension before judgment.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.8.32	Truth as a means of release	The commentary joins truth to freeing a captive; Jesus says knowing the truth will make his hearers free, recasting liberation as an effect of truth.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.23.29	The word as fire and a rock-breaking hammer	The commentary gives truth the image of a straight blow; Jeremiah compares God’s word to fire and a hammer that breaks rock, making truthful speech forceful rather than merely abstract.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.19.26	A dying Jesus entrusts his mother	The commentary’s testament scene gathers approaching death, entrusted care, and a transfer between people; Jesus from the cross gives his mother and the beloved disciple to one another.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.19.27	The entrusted person is received into a home	The commentary says trust and custody meet at death; the disciple takes Mary into his own home, carrying out the deathbed entrustment as practical care.
FOLLOWUP_TSV
"

item.text: I noticed the pledge passage may be one verse earlier in Hebrew numbering. I’m rewriting the follow-up from the remembered draft with that reference corrected, without reading any files.

medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.1.16	Fire consumes accumulated flocks and servants	The commentary’s ruined garden includes a destructive fiery storm; in Job’s sequence of calamities, fire from heaven consumes sheep and servants, one part of the sudden loss of his holdings.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.90.12	Numbering days to gain wisdom	The commentary treats time as expiring capital; the psalm asks to be taught to number one’s days so the heart may gain wisdom, turning limited time into a prompt for action.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.1.2	Meditating on instruction day and night	The commentary says communal counsel joins like night and day; the psalmist meditates on Torah day and night, making ethical instruction a sustained practice across time.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.1.3	A righteous tree bears fruit in season and does not wither	The commentary’s fruitful garden is destroyed at the moment of expected yield; Psalm 1 pictures the righteous as a watered tree whose seasonal fruit remains, a counter-image of stability.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Amos.8.2	Summer fruit announces the end	The commentary layers ripe produce with life’s late hour and the end of time; Amos’s basket of summer fruit signals that Israel’s end has arrived, making harvest itself an omen of ending.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.40.8	Human growth fades while the word endures	The commentary moves from mortal time to truth that is transmitted and kept; Isaiah contrasts fading grass and flowers with the enduring word of God.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.3.3	Truth bound at the neck and written on the heart	The commentary joins truth to holding and binding; Proverbs tells the reader to bind faithfulness and truth around the neck and write them on the heart, combining tethering with inward preservation.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.6.1	A person becomes surety for a neighbor	The commentary gives patience the secondary image of a guarantor and joins trust to debt; Proverbs depicts someone pledging security for a neighbor, making the guarantee a concrete accepted burden.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Exod.22.25	A pledged garment returned before sunset	The commentary joins debt, holding, and release within passing time; Exodus requires a creditor to return a poor borrower’s garment by sunset, so the pledge cannot become lasting captivity.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.15.14	A freed servant sent away with produce	The commentary defines the ascent through freeing a captive and feeding the hungry; Deuteronomy says not to send a released servant away empty-handed but to provide from flock, threshing floor, and winepress.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:2Kgs.4.1	A creditor threatens to take a widow’s sons as slaves	The commentary brings debt and release from captivity together; the widow’s unpaid debt puts her sons at risk of enslavement, making the financial obligation a threat to family freedom.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:2Kgs.4.7	Oil sold to pay debt and preserve a livelihood	The commentary’s debt and release scenes meet in Elisha’s instruction: the widow sells the multiplied oil, pays the creditor, and lives on what remains.
strong	tevrat	motif	Sirach 29:15	Remember the one who stood as guarantor	The commentary calls patience a guarantor; Sirach warns not to forget the kindness of one who guaranteed a neighbor’s debt and risked much on that person’s behalf.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.7.22	Jesus as guarantor of a better covenant	The commentary’s secondary guarantor image meets Hebrews’ explicit description of Jesus as guarantor, applying financial surety language to the covenant.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.1.13	Truth heard, believed, and sealed	The commentary gathers belief, truth, and what is kept; Ephesians says its readers heard the word of truth, believed, and were sealed with the promised Spirit.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.1.14	A seal that guarantees inheritance	The commentary calls patience a guarantor and ends with what is preserved; Ephesians calls the Spirit the guarantee of inheritance until redemption.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.4.2	Patience expressed by bearing with one another	The commentary turns patience into reciprocal communal counsel; Paul joins humility, patience, and bearing with one another in love.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.4.3	Unity held by a bond of peace	The commentary pictures people holding together; Paul urges preservation of the Spirit’s unity through a bond of peace.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.13.6	Love rejoices with truth	The commentary makes truth the content of mutual counsel; Paul says love rejoices with the truth, placing truthful conduct inside communal ethics.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.13.7	Love bears and endures all things	The commentary presents patience as a quality exchanged within the community; Paul describes love as bearing and enduring all things, a sustained communal form of sabr.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.2.7	Patient persistence in good work	The commentary’s exception to loss joins belief, good deeds, and patience; Paul describes those who persist patiently in good work as seeking glory and eternal life.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.3.13	Daily mutual exhortation prevents hardening	The commentary’s community advises one another; Hebrews commands daily encouragement so that no one is hardened by sin’s deceit, specifying both the repeated action and its danger.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.10.36	Endurance after doing God’s will	The commentary closes with good action and patience held together; Hebrews says endurance is needed after doing God’s will in order to receive what is promised.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.12.1	Lay aside weight and run with endurance	The commentary makes the steep ascent a road with a load; Hebrews tells runners to lay aside every weight and run the set race with endurance.
strong	tevrat	motif	Mishnah Avot 4:11	Good deeds as advocates and a shield	The commentary says deeds distinguish those who escape loss; Avot pictures a commandment as an advocate and repentance with good deeds as a shield against punishment.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.119.11	The word stored in the heart	The commentary ends with truth received and preserved; the psalmist stores God’s word in the heart as a safeguard against sin, making inward keeping an ethical act.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.5.16	Time treated as something to redeem	The commentary calls time capital that can be spent or lost; Paul urges believers to make the most of the time because the days are evil, giving time an explicit economic value.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rev.14.19	Ripe grapes cast into the winepress of judgment	The commentary layers fruit, pressing, and the end; Revelation gathers ripe grapes and casts them into God’s great winepress, making the press a harvest image of judgment.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.15.58	Steadfast work is not in vain	The commentary says most human effort is loss but closes with faithful work and patience; Paul calls believers steadfast and abundant in the Lord’s work, assuring them that such labor is not empty.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.13.8	One more year for a fruitless tree	The commentary overlaps orchard, aging time, and the risk of losing fruit; the gardener asks for one more year to tend the barren fig tree, making patience a limited extension before judgment.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.8.32	Truth as a means of release	The commentary joins truth to freeing a captive; Jesus says knowing the truth will make his hearers free, recasting liberation as an effect of truth.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.23.29	The word as fire and a rock-breaking hammer	The commentary gives truth the image of a straight blow; Jeremiah compares God’s word to fire and a hammer that breaks rock, making truthful speech forceful rather than merely abstract.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.19.26	A dying Jesus entrusts his mother	The commentary’s testament scene gathers approaching death, entrusted care, and a transfer between people; Jesus from the cross gives his mother and the beloved disciple to one another.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:John.19.27	The entrusted person is received into a home	The commentary says trust and custody meet at death; the disciple takes Mary into his own home, carrying out the deathbed entrustment as practical care.
